svg.text: Figure 9.1. The Tracer: the RV64 core, its memory interface, and its peripheral side toward C&C 3
v1.3 (planning/DECISIONS-v1.3.md §1–25; DECISIONS-v1.26 items 2, 10, 12; spec §4.17) — block level; the core's inner split is for orientation only
the memory system: a black box (§12, §20, §21)
the translator: a TLB tagged (root, page) and the chip's one tree walker
the shared 512 KB cache (4,096 lines of 128 B, 8-way), LPDDR behind it
C&C 3 (RV32), the Tracer's controller, and its router
the bus: mode-0 writes into the region (0x04), via the director
the register window: 32-bit loads and stores (0xFFFFFA00)
the fill bus: one 128 B line (1,024 bits) per transfer,
a (root, depth, line) request: a program, data or mapping miss
its line; dirty lines at a
the table in a dedicated 128 KB
open: arbitration, blocking, write buffer, error response
the RV64 core (§25): its own core
two lines and two pages: two lookups (§25)
the decode table → the template's words, or
controller-fed ones from the expansion queue;
the next offset; stops after RUN_CYCLES rows
Jolt's rows: ALU, PEXT (any mask, §9), memory
rows; an advice row pops the read queue
the working state: the state record
written through the region, read out by the DMA
the bus from C&C 3: 128-bit writes into the region (§12)
into the core: the state record (§23)
dotted: the expansion tables, loaded once at startup
the register window: RUN_CYCLES, pulses, events, ERRORS (§24)
DMA packets into a router input of its own → the tiles' memory (first implementation, §24)
11 the fill bus: arbitration, blocking, write buffer, errors back
12 the probe's line bound 13 the fetch path's offset subtract
14 the per-stream compression enables 15 bit numbers
17 queue depths, the drain's interleaving 18 bit positions
proposed: suggested, not yet ruled on
The Tracer runs the guest on its own RV64 core. Its instruction cache, data cache and jump LRU are its only local stores; each miss is one 128 B line of a file, (root, depth, line),
on the fill bus to the memory system. One bus from C&C 3 fills the advice and expansion queues, loads the expansion tables once at startup, and writes the state into the core;
the window runs it. At each done the DMA drains the output queues (figure 9.2): the state, read in place, and the three streams. Writing word 0 resets everything.
Source: planning/DECISIONS-v1.3.md (to 7374646) §1–7, 12, 13, 18–25; DECISIONS-v1.26.md items 1, 2, 10, 12; spec/machine-spec.md §4.17, §4.19. Review: WORKER24/NOTES.md.
